title: Assessing the impact of prostaglandin E2 and voltage-gated sodium- or calcium-channels on sensation and local vasodilation upon slowly depolarising electrical nerve fiber stimulation
summary: In the present study, we aim to investigate the sensitizing effect of prostaglandin E2 in healthy volunteers and the functional involvement of the voltage-gated sodium channel 1.8 and voltage-gated calcium channel blockade on electrical and heat stimulation of skin nerve fibers. Slowly stimulating electrical pulses and constant heat activate thin nerve fibers of the skin (C-fibers), which play a central role in the development and maintenance of nerve fiber-mediated (so called "neuropathic") and inflammatory pain conditions. In inflammatory conditions (for example in sunburn) these nerve fibers can sensitize towards mechanical or thermal stimuli. Classical representatives of compounds that are released during inflammation is prostaglandin E2. It was shown before that prostaglandin E2 enhances the capability of the voltage-gated sodium channel 1.8 to open. Mechanistically, this could contribute to axonal sensitization of nerve fibers during inflammation and the importance of voltage-gated sodium channel 1.8 in the therapy of neuropathic pain (for instance with suzetrigine) is currently discussed. At the terminal endings of a particular subgroup of nerve fibers in the skin (so called "silent" C-fibers) the activation of voltage-gated calcium channels evoke the release of mediators (peptides) accompanied with the induction of a local skin reddening. From the obtained results of the present study exploring the pain response and local vasodilation upon electrical and heat stimulation after intradermal injection of prostaglandin E2 and blockers of the voltage-gated sodium channel 1.8 and voltage-gated calcium channels we expect additional information on the neuronal mechanisms and therapeutic perspectives for the treatment of patients with neuropathic pain.
conditions: studying healthy volunteers; Basic research investigating sensitization and modulation of nociceptors in inflammatory condition during inflammation
